simple.meaning: אִגְּרָא (ʼiggᵉrâʼ) is a Hebrew word meaning “an epistle (as carried by a state courier or postman).” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: אִגְּרָא (H104) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Ezra 4:8, with occurrences in Ezra.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אִגְּרָא (H104) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in אִגְּרָא (H104) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: אִגְּרָא (ʼiggᵉrâʼ) / H104 is traced through Ezra 4:8, Ezra 4:11, Ezra 5:6 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

timeline.evidenceText: Rehum the chancellor and Shimshai the scribe wrote a letter against Jerusalem to Artaxerxes the king as follows,
This is the copy of the letter that they sent:
The copy of the letter that Tattenai, the governor beyond the River, and Shetharbozenai, and his companions the Apharsachites, who were beyond the River, sent to Darius the king follows.
